judgment_text:
Prayer Civil Revision Petition filed under Art. 227 of Constitution of India, praying to allow the above Civil Revision Petition by setting aside the Fair and Decretal order dated 8-4-2025 passed in IA No. 686 of 2024 in OS No. 90/2016 on the file of the Additional District Munsif Court, Tiruppur

ORDER

Challenging the impugned order passed in I.A. No. 686 of 2024 in O.S. No. 90 of 2016 by the learned Additional District Munsif, Tiruppur, the Revision Petitioners/Plaintiffs preferred this Civil Revision Petition.

2. Before the trial court, the Revision Petitioners/plaintiffs filed an application under Order I Rule 10 r/w 151 CPC to implead one Kavithamani as proposed defendant, who purchased the property pending suit. On hearing both sides, the trial Judge dismissed the application holding that the case is pending for nearly about 9 years and further, on considering the long delay, the trial court was not inclined to allow the application. Aggrieved over that, the Revision Petitioner/third party preferred this Civil Revision Petition.

3. The learned counsel for Revision Petitioners pointed out that on 22-4-2024, the proposed defendant purchased the property from the 3rd defendant, who remained exparte. Therefore, the revisions petitioners prayed to implead the proposed defendant. But, the trial Judge failed to consider the same and erroneously dismissed the application. Hence, he prayed to set aside the findings of the trial Judge.

4. Heard and considered rival submissions made by both learned counsel for revision petitioners and 5th respondent and perused the materials available on record.

5. Admittedly, the Revision Petitioners filed the suit for the relief of declaration and other consequential relief and the 5th respondent/proposed party is the purchaser. Therefore, she is the necessary party to the proceedings and if she is impleaded, it would not cause any prejudice to the respondents. If opportunity is not given to her, the Revision Petitioners will be put into much hardship. Therefore, the findings rendered in I.A. No. 686 of 2024 in O.S. No. 90 of 2016 by the Additional District Munsif, Tiruppur is set aside. Liberty is granted to the respondents/Defendants 1 to 4 to raise all their defence by filing additional written statement, if any. On hearing both sides, the trial court is directed to proceed with the trial and dispose the case as early as possible. Accordingly, this Civil Revision Petition is allowed. No costs. Consequently, connected civil miscellaneous petition is closed.
